[[slide:greeting]]
Hi Alex and Jordan. This is a short recap of your 2025 federal and Missouri income tax returns, filed jointly. In the next couple of minutes we will walk through what you earned, what you paid in during the year, and why the result came out the way it did.
[[slide:income]]
Your total income for the year was $153,800. Most of that came from wages of $142,500. You also had taxable interest of $1,240, dividends of $3,860, a capital gain of $4,200, and other income of $2,000 reported on Schedule 1.
[[slide:deductions]]
After adjustments to income of $6,500, your adjusted gross income was $147,300. You used the standard deduction of $30,000, which brought your taxable income to $117,300. Itemizing would not have helped this year.
[[slide:tax]]
The income tax on that amount was $15,870. Nonrefundable credits of $2,000 reduced it, and other taxes of $283 were added, for a total federal tax of $14,153. That works out to an effective rate of 12.1% on your taxable income.
[[slide:result]]
Federal withholding from your paychecks came to $17,900, which was more than your total tax. The difference is a federal refund of $3,747. Missouri also came out in your favor: state tax of $5,310 against state withholding of $5,900 leaves a Missouri refund of $590.
[[slide:observations]]
Compared with last year, your adjusted gross income rose by $7,500, an increase of 5.4%. Your total tax was almost unchanged, down $67 from the prior year, and your refund grew by $1,597. Withholding covered 126.5% of your total tax, so a little more than needed was taken out of your pay during the year.
[[slide:next]]
At your review we can talk about whether your withholding still fits your situation for the year ahead, and about anything on the horizon that could change the picture. We look forward to reviewing this with you.
